paragraphs.text: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־פְּנֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ עָלָ֖יו וַיִּשַּׁק־לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yosef fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֨ו יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶת־עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶת־הָרֹ֣פְאִ֔ים לַחֲנֹ֖ט אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וַיַּחַנְט֥וּ הָרֹפְאִ֖ים אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Yosef commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Yisra'el.

paragraphs.commentary:
*La-chanot et-aviv* and *va-yachantu ha-rof'im et-Yisra'el* introduce the chapter's principal Egyptian-mortuary-practice lexeme. The verb *chanat* in the embalming-sense is chapter-singular in HB usage (vv 2, 3, 26 here; the Song 2:13 *chantah* is the unrelated 'ripen' sense). The Hebrew *rof'im* ('physicians') stands in for the Egyptian *wt*-embalmer and *kheri-heb* funerary-priest classes — the technicians and ritual-officiants of the Egyptian-mortuary-rite (Sarna *JPS Genesis* pp. 346-347; Hamilton *NICOT* pp. 692-693; Speiser *Genesis* AB pp. 374-375).

The shift from v 1 *aviv* ('his father' — Yosef's-private-grief) to v 2 *Yisra'el* (the embalmers' subject — the corporate-patriarchal-name) is editorially significant: the institutional-corporate-name governs the formal-embalming-narration. See the cycle-wide central `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-central-promotion` for the cycle-saturating name-shift pattern and the 5-way bidirectional sibling-cluster.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְלְאוּ־לוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י הַחֲנֻטִ֑ים וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ מִצְרַ֖יִם שִׁבְעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those who are embalmed: and the Mitsrim wept for him threescore and ten days.

paragraphs.commentary:
The Egyptian-mortuary numerology: 40-day embalming + 70-day total mourning. The numerology matches the documented Egyptian-royal-funerary-mourning-period (40-day natron-drying-and-wrapping embalming + 30-day post-embalmment ritual = 70 total). The classical-Egyptological apparatus: Herodotus 2.86-90 (the three classes of embalming-treatment); Diodorus Siculus 1.91 (the 30-day post-embalmment mourning); Plutarch *De Iside* 13 (the Osiris-mortuary-numerology); Sarna *JPS Genesis* pp. 346-347; Hamilton *NICOT* pp. 692-693; Taylor *Death and the Afterlife in Ancient Egypt* 2001.

The 70-day-figure brackets the Yosef-cycle's seventy-cluster opened at Gen 46:27 (*kol ha-nefesh le-veit Ya'aqov ha-ba'ah Mitsraymah shiv'im*): the cycle's entry-bookend (the nephesh-count seventy at the descent) and the cycle's closing-bookend (the embalming-mourning-days seventy here) frame the cycle's Egyptian-residence narrative (Sarna pp. 318-319, 346-347).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י בְכִית֔וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶל־בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם דַּבְּרוּ־נָ֕א בְּאָזְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And when the days of weeping for him were past, Yosef spake unto the house of Par'oh, saying, If now I have found favor in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Par'oh, saying,

paragraphs.commentary: *El-beit Par'oh* ('unto the house of Pharaoh') deploys the indirection-construction: Yosef addresses Pharaoh's court rather than Pharaoh directly. Three named-scholarship reading-camps account for the indirection: (i) the mourning-ritual-constraint reading (Yosef's mourning-state restricted his royal-presence-access; Sarna pp. 346-347; Hamilton p. 692); (ii) the Egyptian-court-protocol reading (the *beit Par'oh* idiom denotes the Egyptian *peru-aa* 'great house' court-administration; Speiser pp. 374-375; Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* SVT 20 1970); (iii) the literary-narrative reading (the indirection is narrative-economical, structurally separating the family-mourning-narrative from the political-narrative; Westermann pp. 200-201; Brueggemann p. 374).

paragraphs.text: אָבִ֞י הִשְׁבִּיעַ֣נִי לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ מֵת֒ בְּקִבְרִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן שָׁ֖מָּה תִּקְבְּרֵ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶֽעֱלֶה־נָּ֛א וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה אֶת־אָבִ֖י וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃

i18n.en: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Kena'an, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.

paragraphs.commentary: *Be-qivri asher karithi li* ('in my grave which I have digged for me') raises a narrative-historical crux: Gen 49:29-32 had Ya'aqov instructing burial in the Makhpelah which Avraham purchased; here the reported-speech says *karithi li* ('I have digged for me'). Three named-scholarship reading-camps: (i) the literary-compression reading (the *karithi* is used loosely for 'prepared / acquired'; Sarna p. 347; Alter p. 296); (ii) the supplemental Ya'aqov-grave-preparation reading (Ya'aqov is reported to have done additional preparation-work on the Makhpelah; Hamilton pp. 691-692; the Jubilees-Targumic-Midrashic expansion-tradition preserves this reading); (iii) the source-critical-variant reading (the verse preserves an independent Ya'aqov-dug-grave tradition harmonized with the Makhpelah by the redactor; Westermann pp. 201-202; classical Wellhausenite source-critical).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֑ה עֲלֵ֛ה וּקְבֹ֥ר אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיעֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And Par'oh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל יוֹסֵ֖ף לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וַיַּֽעֲל֨וּ אִתּ֜וֹ כָּל־עַבְדֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בֵית֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל זִקְנֵ֥י אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Yosef went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Par'oh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Mitsrayim,

paragraphs.text: וְכֹל֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאֶחָ֖יו וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו רַ֗ק טַפָּם֙ וְצֹאנָ֣ם וּבְקָרָ֔ם עָזְב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

i18n.en: and all the house of Yosef, and his brethren, and his father's house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַל עִמּ֔וֹ גַּם־רֶ֖כֶב גַּם־פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Gam-rekhev gam-parashim* ('both chariots and horsemen') deploys the corpus's standard military-cavalry vocabulary in the funeral-procession context. Named scholarship reads the lexical-pair as a deliberate literary-anticipation of the Exod 14 Pharaoh's-pursuit-army deployment, where the same vocabulary saturates the Reed-Sea-pursuit narrative (Exod 14:9, 17, 23, 26, 28: *kol-sus rekhev Par'oh u-farashav*). The Gen 50:9 funeral-procession and the Exod 14 pursuit-army deploy the same chariots-and-horsemen vocabulary at opposite ends of the Egyptian-Hebrew-relations narrative-arc — the Genesis-end honor-cortege foreshadowing the Exodus-pursuit-army (Sarna pp. 348-349; Brueggemann pp. 374-375; Sternberg *Poetics of Biblical Narrative* pp. 285-286; Alter p. 297).

The observation is one of three converging Genesis-to-Exodus narrative-forward-bridge clusters; see overlay `genesis-50-as-narrative-forward-bridge-to-exodus-meta-observation` for the chapter-level architecture.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַד־גֹּ֣רֶן הָאָטָ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּ֨סְפְּדוּ־שָׁ֔ם מִסְפֵּ֛ד גָּד֥וֹל וְכָבֵ֖ד מְאֹ֑ד וַיַּ֧עַשׂ לְאָבִ֛יו אֵ֖בֶל שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And they came to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond the Yarden, and there they lamented with a very great and sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Goren ha-Atad* ('the threshing-floor of Atad / the bramble') beyond the Yarden is the funeral-cortege's eastern-Yarden mourning-stop. The verse deploys the *misped gadol ve-khaved me'od* ('very great and sore lamentation') intensified-superlative formula, one of the corpus's most-intensified mourning-rite expressions. The *misped* lexeme is the HB's principal formal-lamentation-vocabulary (cross-corpus Jer 6:26; Amos 5:16; Mic 1:8; Zech 12:10-11 *misped gadol bi-Yerushalayim*; cf. central `misped-lamentation-vocabulary-cross-corpus`).

*Evel shiv'at yamim* ('a mourning for his father seven days') deploys the seven-day-mourning institution — the antecedent of the rabbinic *shiv'ah*-tradition (b. Mo'ed Qatan 20a explicitly derives the *shiv'ah*-rite from this verse). Cross-corpus 1 Sam 31:13 (Sha'ul-Yonatan); 1 Chr 10:12; Sir 22:12; Judith 16:24. The Hebrew seven-day-mourning is here deployed alongside the Egyptian 70-day-mourning of v 3 — the chapter brackets the dual mourning-rite traditions, Egyptian-and-Hebrew (Sarna pp. 348-349; Alter p. 298; Anderson *A Time to Mourn, A Time to Dance* 1991; Olyan *Biblical Mourning* 2004).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֡רְא יוֹשֵׁב֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֜י אֶת־הָאֵ֗בֶל בְּגֹ֙רֶן֙ הָֽאָטָ֔ד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵֽבֶל־כָּבֵ֥ד זֶ֖ה לְמִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ אָבֵ֣ל מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Kena'ani, saw the mourning at the threshing-floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Mitsrim: wherefore the name of it was called Avel-Mitsrayim, which is beyond the Yarden.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Avel-Mitzrayim* ('Avel of the Mitsrim') is one of Genesis's principal aetiological-toponyms. The naming deploys a Hebrew paronomasia between *evel* ('mourning') and *avel* ('meadow / watercourse-marsh'): the surface-sense reads 'meadow of Egypt' (the *avel*-element appears in other toponyms — Avel-Beit-Ma'akhah, Avel-Mechola); the homophonous-echo reads 'mourning of Egypt' as the chapter explicitly stages via the *evel-khaved ze le-Mitsrayim* etymology (Sarna p. 349; Hamilton pp. 695-696; Alter p. 298; Westermann pp. 203-204).

The *al-ken qara shemah* ('wherefore the name of it was called') formula is the corpus's canonical aetiological-naming-formula, saturating Genesis (Bavel, Be'er-Lachai-Roi, Tzo'ar, Be'er-Sheva, Yahweh-Yireh, Beit-El, Sukkot, et al.) and recurring across Exod, Num, Josh, Judg, Sam, Kgs. See central `al-ken-qara-shemah-aetiological-naming-formula-cross-corpus` for the corpus-saturating distribution.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בָנָ֖יו ל֑וֹ כֵּ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽם׃

i18n.en: And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ בָנָיו֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בִּמְעָרַ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָה֩ אַבְרָהָ֨ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה לַאֲחֻזַּת־קֶ֗בֶר מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃

i18n.en: for his sons carried him into the land of Kena'an, and buried him in the cave of the field of Makhpelah, which Avraham bought with the field for a possession of a burying-place from Efron the Chitti, before Mamre.

paragraphs.commentary: The Makhpelah-burial closure of the patriarchal-burial-cycle. The verse rehearses the Gen 23 land-acquisition (Avraham's purchase of the field from Efron the Chitti at Mamre / Hebron) and completes the patriarchal-burial-cluster: Avraham + Sarah + Yitzchaq + Rivqah + Le'ah + Ya'aqov (per Gen 49:31). The *achuzzat-qever* ('possession of a burying-place') formula echoes Gen 23:9 + 23:20 + Gen 49:30 — the *achuzzah*-keyword tying the patriarchal-land-possession theme together across the cycle (Sarna pp. 347-348; Hamilton pp. 696-697; Westermann pp. 204-205).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יוֹסֵ֤ף מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ ה֣וּא וְאֶחָ֔יו וְכָל־הָעֹלִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֑יו אַחֲרֵ֖י קָבְר֥וֹ אֶת־אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Yosef returned into Mitsrayim, he, and his brethren, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֲחֵֽי־יוֹסֵף֙ כִּי־מֵ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ ל֥וּ יִשְׂטְמֵ֖נוּ יוֹסֵ֑ף וְהָשֵׁ֤ב יָשִׁיב֙ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּמַ֖לְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And when Yosef's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, It may be that Yosef will hate us, and will fully requite us all the evil which we did unto him.

paragraphs.commentary: The brothers' fear-expression: *lu yistemenu Yosef ve-hashev yashiv lanu et kol-ha-ra'ah asher gamalnu oto* ('It may be that Yosef will hate us, and will fully requite us all the evil which we did unto him'). Three compounded vocabulary observations: (i) *lu* the apprehensive-conditional particle ('perhaps / what if'; named scholarship reads the deployment as the apprehensive 'perhaps' sense rather than the wishful 'if only'); (ii) *hashev yashiv* the emphatic-paronomastic infinitive-absolute + finite construction (one of the HB's standard intensification-patterns; sibling-link to Gen 37:33 *tarof toraf* — the cycle's foundational evil-anticipation paronomastic-construction; the cycle opens with Ya'aqov's evil-anticipation paronomastic-construction at Gen 37:33 and closes with the brothers' at Gen 50:15; Sarna p. 350; Alter p. 298; Sternberg pp. 285-308); (iii) *gamal* the requital-verb (deployed both here and at v 17 *gemalukha*; cf. cross-corpus Deut 32:6; Pss 7:5, 13:6, 103:10; Prov 3:30, 31:12).

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַוּ֕וּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֣יךָ צִוָּ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹת֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And they sent a message unto Yosef, saying, Thy father did command before he died, saying,

paragraphs.commentary: *Avikha tzivah lifnei moto lemor* ('thy father did command before he died, saying...') raises the literary-critical fabrication-crux: the narrative does not record any such Ya'aqov-instruction during the prior chapters (Gen 47-49). Three named-scholarship reading-camps: (i) the dominant fabrication-reading (the brothers fabricate the instruction to invoke their father's authority; Sarna pp. 350-351; Alter p. 299; Brueggemann pp. 376-377; Hamilton pp. 698-699); (ii) the narrative-ellipsis reading (the instruction did occur but the narrator did not include it; the traditional-Jewish reading, including Rashi's *meshanim mi-pnei ha-shalom* tradition); (iii) the deliberate-narrative-ambiguity reading (the historicity is intentionally unresolvable; Sternberg *Poetics* pp. 285-308; Alter *Art of Biblical Narrative* pp. 153-156). Yosef's response at vv 17-21 notably does not address the historicity-question.

paragraphs.text: כֹּֽה־תֹאמְר֣וּ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף אָ֣נָּ֡א שָׂ֣א נָ֠א פֶּ֣שַׁע אַחֶ֤יךָ וְחַטָּאתָם֙ כִּי־רָעָ֣ה גְמָל֔וּךָ וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א נָ֔א לְפֶ֥שַׁע עַבְדֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ יוֹסֵ֖ף בְּדַבְּרָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: So shall ye say unto Yosef, Forgive, I pray thee now, the transgression of thy brethren, and their sin, for that they did unto thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the transgression of the servants of the Elohim of thy father. And Yosef wept when they spake unto him.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Sa na pesha achei-kha ve-chatta'tam* + *sa na le-fesha avdei Elohei avikha* deploys the *nasa-pesha/avon* ('lift up / forgive transgression') formula twice in a single verse — one of the HB's principal forgiveness-vocabulary formulas. The formula reaches its canonical-doctrinal articulation at Exod 34:6-7 (the divine-attribute formula *nose avon va-fesha ve-chatta'ah*, basis of the rabbinic *Shelosh Esreh Middot* 'Thirteen Attributes of Mercy' liturgical tradition) and recurs across the corpus's penitential and divine-attribute deployments (Num 14:18; Ps 32:1+5; Mic 7:18; Isa 33:24; Job 7:21; Hos 14:3). The brothers' deployment is the formula's earliest narrative-occurrence in the corpus (Sarna p. 351; Hamilton p. 699; Alter p. 299; Brueggemann p. 377; Childs *Exodus* OTL pp. 612-617 on the Exod 34 articulation).

The *avdei Elohei avikha* ('servants of the Elohim of thy father') closes the petition with the patriarchal-Elohim register. *Va-yevk Yosef be-dabberam elav* ('and Yosef wept when they spake unto him') — the chapter's third weeping-occurrence (vv 1, 17 here, with the implicit Yosef-emotion-discharge cluster continuing the Gen 42-45 weeping-pattern).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ גַּם־אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ הִנֶּ֥נּֽוּ לְךָ֖ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we are thy servants.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yippelu lefanav* ('they fell down before him') closes the Gen 37 sheaves-and-stars dream-fulfilment arc. The five prior explicit *hishtachavah* events of the dream-fulfilment cycle (Gen 42:6, 43:26, 43:28, 44:14, and the implicit Gen 37:7+9+10 dream-anticipations) culminate at v 18 in the brothers' final prostration before Yosef after Ya'aqov's death. The chapter does not deploy the explicit *hishtachavah* lexeme but the *va-yippelu* fall-down construction implies it; named scholarship reads v 18 as the narrative-completion of the dream-fulfilment-bowing-sequence even with the lexical-shift (Sarna p. 351; Alter p. 299; Hamilton p. 699; Brueggemann p. 376). See central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ כִּ֛י הֲתַ֥חַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים אָֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of Elohim?

paragraphs.commentary: *Ki ha-tachat Elohim ani* ('for am I in the place of Elohim?') — Yosef's rhetorical refusal of the judge-role. The deployment of *tachat* in its substitution-sense ('in the place of / instead of') closes the Yosef-cycle's substitution-arc: at Gen 44:33 Yehudah offers to substitute for the lad (the cycle's moral-climax substitution-offer); at Gen 50:19 Yosef rhetorically refuses to substitute for Elohim (the cycle's theological-climax substitution-refusal). The bidirectional Gen 44:33 ↔ Gen 50:19 sibling-link is the substitution-formula's Yosef-cycle internal-architecture (Sarna pp. 351-352; Alter p. 300; Brueggemann p. 377). See central `tachat-substitution-formula`.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתֶּ֕ם חֲשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָלַ֖י רָעָ֑ה אֱלֹהִים֙ חֲשָׁבָ֣הּ לְטֹבָ֔ה לְמַ֗עַן עֲשֹׂ֛ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֥ת עַם־רָֽב׃

i18n.en: And as for you, ye meant evil against me; but Elohim meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

paragraphs.commentary:
**THE CHAPTER'S THEOLOGICAL CLIMAX** — *ve-attem chashavtem alay ra'ah Elohim chashavah le-tovah lema'an asoh ka-yom ha-zeh le-hachayot am-rav* ('as for you, ye meant evil against me; but Elohim meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive'). The verse stages the climactic-completion of the Yosef-cycle's providential-reframing-arc — the same theological-reframing-of-the-brothers'-evil expressed at Gen 45:5-8 *shelachani Elohim lifneikhem* ('Elohim sent me before you'), here in its canonical *chashavtem ra'ah / chashavah le-tovah* explicit evil-becomes-good chiastic-paronomasia.

The construction's paronomastic-doubling — *chashavtem* (human-subject, perfective) / *chashavah* (divine-subject, perfective + 3fs-suffix referring to the *ra'ah* the brothers reckoned) — is one of the corpus's most-quoted verbal-pivots, with the same root *chashav* ('to reckon / intend / devise') governing both subjects and the antithetical-pair *ra'ah* / *le-tovah* naming the reframing. The Gen 50:20 formulation makes explicit what Gen 45 left implicit: the brothers' Gen 37 sale was *ra'ah* (evil), and the providential-reframing names the divine-reckoning-as-good as standing alongside (not erasing) the human-reckoning-as-evil (Sarna pp. 350-351; Alter p. 299; Brueggemann pp. 376-377; von Rad pp. 432-433).

The verse closes the chayah-keyword arc: Gen 45:5 *le-michyah* → 45:7 *u-le-hachayot lakhem li-pleitah gedolah* → 45:27 *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* → 47:25 *hechyitanu* → 50:20 *le-hachayot am-rav*. The cycle-saturating *chayah*-root preserves the preservation-of-life keyword across the cycle (see sibling central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`).

The Gen 45 ↔ Gen 50:20 bidirectional sibling-pair is the project's central-to-central pair for the providential-reframing-arc. The chapter's reception-history reach (the Esther reversal-narrative's implicit theological structure; the Romans 8:28 Christian reception; the rabbinic *gam zu le-tovah* tradition) is documented at the central `atem-chashavtem-elohim-chashavah-le-tovah-providential-reframing-climax-gen50` as reception-only — **no Christian-soteriological pre-resolution; no Calvinistic-compatibilist adjudication; no WoH spin on divine providence**.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אוּ אָנֹכִ֛י אֲכַלְכֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־טַפְּכֶ֑ם וַיְנַחֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־לִבָּֽם׃

i18n.en: Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Anokhi akhalkel etkhem ve-et tappekhem* ('I will nourish you, and your little ones') restates the Yosef-cycle's sustenance-promise (Gen 45:11; 47:12) — see central `kalkel-yosef-sustenance-promise-gen45-46-47-50` for the cycle-saturating promise's chapter-cluster. The chapter's final *taph* deployment (cf. v 8 *taphkhem*) is the cycle's closing little-ones-dependents-class reference.

*Va-yenachem otam va-yedabber al-libbam* ('and he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them') closes the reconciliation-scene with two consolation-formulae: the *nichem* 'comfort' verb and the *dabber al-lev* 'speak to the heart' formula. The *dabber al-lev* construction is the HB's principal idiom for consoling, kindly-persuading, or reassuring-speech directed at a person's emotional core (cross-corpus Gen 34:3; Judg 19:3; Ruth 2:13; 2 Sam 19:8; 2 Chr 30:22, 32:6; Isa 40:2 *dabberu al-lev Yerushalayim*; Hos 2:16 *ve-dibbarti al-libbah*).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יוֹסֵף֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם ה֖וּא וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו וַיְחִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Yosef dwelt in Mitsrayim, he, and his father's house: and Yosef lived a hundred and ten years.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yechi Yosef me'ah va-eser shanim* ('and Yosef lived a hundred and ten years'). 110 was the Egyptian-ideal-lifespan, attested in over thirty Egyptian funerary inscriptions in the *deba renpit* ('one hundred ten years') formula from the Middle Kingdom through the Late Period — the Egyptian ideal of a fulfilled-and-complete life (Janssen, 'On the Ideal Lifetime of the Egyptians' OMRO 31 [1950] 33-43; Sarna p. 355; Hamilton pp. 706-707; Speiser p. 378). Yosef's lifespan signals his full-acculturation to Egyptian life — he has lived the ideal Egyptian span and will die in Mitsrayim under Egyptian funerary-rite (v 26).

Cross-corpus Josh 24:29 records Yehoshua's identical 110-year lifespan: *ben-me'ah va-eser shanim* — read by named scholarship as a deliberate literary-bridge between the Egyptian-acculturated Yosef (Gen 50:22) and the Promised-Land-conquest leader Yehoshua (Josh 24:29). The figure forms a numerical-architectural arc across the Egyptian-acculturation and Promised-Land-settlement narratives (Sarna p. 355; Boling *Joshua* AB pp. 540-541; Nelson *Joshua* OTL pp. 281-282).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֤רְא יוֹסֵף֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּנֵ֖י שִׁלֵּשִׁ֑ים גַּ֗ם בְּנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יֻלְּד֖וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵּ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And Yosef saw Ephraim's children of the third generation: the children also of Makhir the son of Menasheh were born upon Yosef's knees.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yar Yosef le-Efraim bnei shilleshim* ('and Yosef saw Efraim's children of the third generation') — Yosef's grandchildren and great-grandchildren in the third-generation line.

*Gam bnei Makhir ben-Menasheh yulledu al-birkei Yosef* ('the children also of Makhir the son of Menasheh were born upon Yosef's knees') — the *al-birkei Yosef* adoption-on-the-knees ritual at the third generation. The deployment is the sibling-closure of the Gen 48:12 knees-ritual: Ya'aqov receives Yosef's sons on his knees at Gen 48:12 (the cycle's opening knees-ritual); Yosef receives his great-grandchildren-via-Makhir on his knees at Gen 50:23 (the cycle's closing knees-ritual). Cross-corpus Ruth 4:16 (Na'omi-Obed knees-and-bosom ritual). The bidirectional Gen 48:12 ↔ Gen 50:23 sibling-link is the chapter-internal adoption-knees-ritual's pair-architecture (Sarna p. 354; Hamilton pp. 705-706; Alter p. 300; Westermann pp. 206-207). See overlay `bein-birkav-adoption-on-the-knees-ritual-gen48`.

**Makhir ben-Menasheh** is the patriarch of the Machirite half-Menasshite clan with extensive Mosaic-and-Joshuanic narrative-tradition (Num 26:29 census; Num 32:39-40 Gil'ad-conquest; Josh 13:31 + 17:1-6 trans-Yarden tribal-allotment; Judg 5:14 Deborah-Song's *mini Makhir yardu mechoqeqim* military-tradition). The clan-eponym's introduction here is the cycle's narrative-forward-bridge into the Mosaic tribal-system (Noth *Das System der zwölf Stämme Israels* 1930; Na'aman *Borders and Districts in Biblical Historiography* 1986).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־אֶחָ֔יו אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים פָּקֹ֧ד יִפְקֹ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֗ם וְהֶעֱלָ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֛ע לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his brethren, I die; but Elohim will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land unto the land which he sware to Avraham, to Yitzchaq, and to Ya'aqov.

paragraphs.commentary:
**THE EXODUS-OPENING KEYWORD FORMULA INTRODUCED.** *Elohim paqod yiphqod etkhem* ('Elohim will surely visit you') deploys the *paqod yiphqod* infinitive-absolute + finite construction — the principal Genesis-to-Exodus narrative-bridge keyword. The formula recurs verbatim at Exod 3:16 (Mosheh's Burning-Bush commission: *paqod paqadti etkhem*); Exod 4:31 (the Israelites' acceptance: *va-yishma'u ki-faqad YHWH*); Exod 13:19 (Mosheh at the Exodus-departure carrying Yosef's bones: *paqod yiphqod Elohim etkhem ve-ha'alitem et-atzmotai mi-zeh ittekhem* — a near-verbatim quotation of Gen 50:25). The Exod 13:19 deployment is the corpus's principal narrative-quotation-anchor between Genesis and Exodus (Sarna pp. 357-358; Childs *Exodus* OTL pp. 1-10, 88-89; Brueggemann pp. 378-380; Houtman *Exodus* HCOT 1:364-365). See central `paqod-yiphqod-divine-visitation-exodus-formula-cross-corpus`.

**The patriarchal-oath triple-formula introduced.** *Ha-aretz asher nishba la-Avraham le-Yitzchaq u-le-Ya'aqov* ('the land which he sware to Avraham, to Yitzchaq, and to Ya'aqov') is the corpus's earliest narrative-occurrence as a closed-three-name formulaic-unit. The formula saturates the Pentateuch (Exod 6:8; 33:1; Num 32:11; Deut 1:8; 6:10; 9:5; 29:13; 30:20; 34:4) and recurs across Joshua and the prophets (Josh 1:6; 24:3; Jer 11:5; Mic 7:20; Ps 105:9) — the principal canonical-formulaic-anchor of the patriarchal-land-promise (Weinfeld *Deuteronomy and the Deuteronomic School* 1972 pp. 75-78; Clines *The Theme of the Pentateuch* JSOTSup 10 1978; Schmid *Genesis and the Moses Story* Siphrut 3 2010). See central `nishba-la-avraham-le-yitzchaq-u-le-yaaqov-patriarchal-oath-triple-formula-cross-corpus`.

**Lens-discipline.** No Christian-eschatological pre-resolution; no WoH temporal-cycle spin; no theological-typological adjudication of the Genesis-to-Exodus bridge.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִתֶ֥ם אֶת־עַצְמֹתַ֖י מִזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef took an oath of the children of Yisra'el, saying, Elohim will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yashba Yosef et-bnei Yisra'el lemor paqod yiphqod Elohim etkhem ve-ha'alitem et-atzmotai mi-zeh* — **Yosef's bones for the Exodus**. The cycle's final words are an Exodus-promise + a bones-instruction, quoted verbatim at Exod 13:19 when Mosheh carries Yosef's bones out of Mitsrayim at the Exodus-departure. The bones-journey continues to Josh 24:32, where the bones are buried at Shechem in the parcel of ground Ya'aqov purchased at Gen 33:19 — a multi-generation arc: Gen 33:19 land-purchase → Gen 50:25 bones-instruction → Exod 13:19 bones-departure → Josh 24:32 bones-burial-at-Shechem (Sarna p. 357; Childs *Exodus* OTL pp. 224-225; Hamilton pp. 707-708; Westermann pp. 209-211).

The Yosef-cycle's narrative-closure remains **deliberately un-resolved**: Yosef's bones are in an Egyptian coffin awaiting the Exodus; the book of Genesis ends with that unresolved tension propelling the rest of the Torah (Alter pp. 300-301; Brueggemann pp. 378-380; Clines *The Theme of the Pentateuch* JSOTSup 10 1978 pp. 47-60; Schmid *Genesis and the Moses Story* Siphrut 3 2010). See central `atzmot-yosef-bones-for-exodus-narrative-forward-bridge-cross-corpus`.

**Lens-discipline.** The bones-journey is documented as named literary-and-comparative scholarship; no Christian-typological reading of the bones as resurrection-anticipation applied — that is reception, not exegesis. The ANE comparative-bones-relic tradition (the Egyptian *kheri-heb* funerary tradition; the Mesopotamian *kispu* ancestor-cult; the Greek *hosta* hero-relic tradition — bones-of-Orestes at Hdt 1.67-68; bones-of-Theseus at Plut. *Cim* 8) is documented at the central.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣מָת יוֹסֵ֔ף בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִ֑ים וַיַּחַנְט֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַיִּ֥ישֶׂם בָּאָר֖וֹן בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: So Yosef died, being a hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yamot Yosef ben-me'ah va-eser shanim va-yachantu oto va-yisem ba-aron be-Mitsrayim* — **the closing verse of Genesis**. Yosef dies at the Egyptian-ideal 110-year lifespan; is embalmed per Egyptian-mortuary-practice (the chapter's second *chanat*-occurrence, bracketing with the Ya'aqov-embalming at vv 2-3); and is placed in an *aron* in Mitsrayim.

The *aron* lexeme here is in its Egyptian-mummy-case sense — most-likely the wooden inner-coffin of the multi-layered Egyptian coffin-system (the *suhet*-outer-coffin / *wet*-inner-coffin / cartonnage-mummy-case architecture; Taylor *Death and the Afterlife in Ancient Egypt* 2001 pp. 214-242; Sarna pp. 355-356; Hamilton p. 707). Named scholarship reads the lexeme's chapter-singular Egyptian-coffin sense as in deliberate-contrast with the later *aron ha-berit / aron ha-edut* (ark of the covenant / testimony) cultic deployments (Exod 25:10+; Num 10:33+; Deut 10:1-5+; 1 Sam 4-6; 2 Sam 6; 1 Kgs 8): the Gen 50:26 *aron* in Mitsrayim awaits the Exodus; the Sinai *aron ha-edut* mediates the covenantal-relationship at the Mosaic-cycle's-center (Brueggemann pp. 378-380; Childs *Exodus* OTL pp. 538-540).

**The closing-frame as deliberate un-resolved-closure.** The book of Genesis ends with the un-buried Yosef in his Egyptian coffin — the symbol of the un-realized patriarchal-promise. The closing-frame's structural-tension propels the rest of the Torah: the *paqod yiphqod* visitation-promise (v 24), the bones-journey (v 25), and the *aron be-Mitsrayim* image (v 26) are all deliberately un-resolved. Named scholarship reads this as one of the corpus's most-celebrated literary-architectural devices — a closure that is not a closure (Sarna p. 358; Alter pp. 300-301; Brueggemann pp. 378-380; von Rad pp. 432-434; Clines *The Theme of the Pentateuch* JSOTSup 10 1978 pp. 47-60; Schmid *Genesis and the Moses Story* Siphrut 3 2010).

**The Genesis-cycle's closing word.** *Be-Mitsrayim*. The book of Genesis ends in Mitsrayim, with the patriarchal-promise un-fulfilled and the corporate-Yisra'el outside the land of promise. The forward-bridge into Exodus is built into the closing-frame's deliberate-tension.
